items.title: Man dies after motorcycle hits fallen tree on Kuala Terengganu–Kota Bharu road in Setiu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — A permanent resident Indonesian man died after his motorcycle crashed into a fallen tree along Jalan Kampung Merang on the Kuala Terengganu–Kota Bharu coastal route late last night. Bernama reported that the victim, identified as 68‑year‑old construction worker Darman Khamis, was believed to be travelling from Kuala Terengganu towards Kampung Bari Besar when the crash occurred. Setiu district police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the accident at about 12.10am from the Setiu district police traffic complaint counter.

items.title: Predawn robbery at Miri mini market leaves worker with injuries, police nab three Malaysian suspects
items.summary: MIRI, Aug 23 — A quiet early morning at a Tudan mini-market turned violent when three men allegedly broke into the premises, attacked an employee and fled with cash and other items. “The victim suffered injuries to her hand and shoulder before receiving treatment at Miri Hospital,” Miri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah was quoted as saying. Police later arrested three Malaysian men aged between 28 and 39, acting on information received and conducting follow-up investigations.

items.title: Four detained in suspected illegal gold mining operation
items.summary: General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the four men, aged between 19 and 64, were detained during the operation at 4pm. He said the operation was carried out by the brigade's intelligence team following information on suspected illegal gold mining activities, with assistance from the Bukit Aman Air Operations Team and Kelantan Land and Mines Office enforcement officers. They comprised two excavators worth about RM1 million, two sluice boxes (RM60,000), two suction machines (RM25,000), two generator sets (RM25,000), 51 pieces of grass carpet (RM10,200) and three rolls of grass carpet (RM15,000).

items.title: Ten undocumented migrants escape from Tanah Merah detention depot
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Ten undocumented migrants escaped from the Immigration detention depot in Tanah Merah early today, prompting police to launch an operation to track them down. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the escapees comprised seven Thai citizens, an Indonesian, a Bangladeshi and a Rohingya. Those with information can contact the Tanah Merah district police headquarters at 09-9556222, Tanah Merah police station at 09-9556223 or the District Control Centre via WhatsApp at 011-29555518.

items.title: Schools in 10 Sarawak districts to resume classes tomorrow as API improves
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 23 — All primary and secondary schools under the 10 District Education Offices (PPDs) in Sarawak will operate as usual from tomorrow, following improvements in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. The Sarawak State Education Department (JPNS) said the schools under the PPDs of Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu and Betong would reopen as scheduled. JPNS reminded schools to take precautionary measures if haze affects their respective areas.

items.title: Orang Asli youth killed after motorcycle hits civet, crashes into SUV
items.summary: Zaki Abu, 19, a plantation worker from Kampung Gadak, Muadzam Shah, died at the scene in the 8.40pm accident. District police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the accident involved Zaki's Honda motorcycle and an SUV driven by a 40-year-old plantation assistant manager. He said Zaki died at the scene, while the SUV driver was unhurt.

items.title: Umno to send representative to Pas Muktamar, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno has confirmed it will send a representative to the 72nd Pas Muktamar in Kelantan next month. Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, however, did not name the representative, saying the party would decide on the matter later. Yesterday, Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan confirmed that invitations had been extended to Zahid and three other Umno leaders to attend the annual gathering.

items.title: EMGS: International students generate RM20b a year for Malaysia’s economy, each contributing an estimated RM10,000 monthly
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 23 — The presence of about 167,000 international students in Malaysia currently contributes around RM20 billion annually to the country’s economy through spending on tuition fees and living expenses, said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) chief executive officer (CEO) Novie Tajuddin. He said Malaysia aims to attract 500,000 international students by 2035, as outlined in the 10-year Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint. “We currently have 167,000 international students.

items.title: MEF: Digital foreign worker system must deliver results, not just go paperless
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The digitalisation of foreign worker recruitment must deliver real improvements, not merely replace paper forms with online ones, the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) said. President Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said digitalising applications through the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS) was a step in the right direction, but its success would depend on execution. Syed Hussain said the goal should be a "one application, one system, one status" approach, where employers need not repeatedly submit the same information to different agencies or make physical visits just to check an application's status.

items.title: Malaysia Smelting mine suspension seen temporary, no outlook hit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Smelting Corp Bhd's (MSC) temporary suspension of mining operations is unlikely to derail its overall outlook, according to Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest). Analyst Denny Oh said the suspension at MSC's 80 per cent-owned Rahman Hydraulic Tin Sdn Bhd in Perak was a temporary operational setback. However, Oh said the impact would be partly cushioned by MSC's tin smelting operations, which remain unaffected as the company can source ore from other mines.

items.title: Malakoff recovery clouded by tax hit; analysts split on outlook
items.summary: RHB Research analyst Max Koh said Malakoff's financial year 2026 earnings estimates had been cut by 45 per cent to account for a higher effective tax rate (ETR) of 40 per cent, compared with 19 per cent previously. "We have adopted a prudent approach by applying a 40 per cent ETR for FY26F," Koh said, adding that the ETR assumptions for FY27 and FY28 had also been raised to 28 per cent from 21 per cent. Prai achieved an energy availability factor of 91 per cent and a capacity factor of 30 per cent in Q2 FY26, contributing RM90 million to group revenue during the quarter.

items.title: Johor Plantations earnings tied to 2H output recovery, CPO prices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Plantations Group Bhd's (JPG) earnings outlook is expected to hinge on a recovery in fresh fruit bunches (FFB) production in the second half (2H) of 2026 and sustained crude palm oil (CPO) prices, following a weaker-than-expected first-half performance. RHB Research analyst Hoe Lee Leng said JPG's FFB production was expected to recover in 2H in line with the seasonal production peak, while higher CPO prices would be positive for the group given its high sensitivity to movements in CPO prices. Chye said JPG's weaker-than-expected earnings had prompted it to lower its FY26 and FY27 core earnings forecasts by 15 per cent and 7.7 per cent, respectively.

items.title: Shifting from 'Made in Malaysia' to 'Made by Malaysians'
items.summary: KUCHING: Malaysia needs to shift from being merely a production base to becoming a country that creates and owns content and intellectual property (IP) to ensure its digital creative industry remains competitive regionally and globally. Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) chief executive officer Anuar Fariz Fadzil said Malaysia could no longer rely on competitive costs as its main strategy to attract and retain the digital content industry. Anuar said Malaysia's strengths included competitive operating costs, English proficiency, local talent and infrastructure capable of supporting international companies.

items.title: Police probe viral video of motorcyclists allegedly racing on Linkedua Highway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating a viral video showing two motorcyclists allegedly racing each other along the Linkedua Highway yesterday. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) said a report was received regarding the incident, which is believed to have occurred from the Senai Utara Toll Interchange towards the JPO Interchange. Previously, a 30-second video went viral on social media showing several motorcyclists blocking other motorists on the highway while others appeared to be racing.

items.title: Allegedly struck with shoe and pencil case: Penang Education Dept steps in after 12-year-old cries assault by teacher in class
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 23 — The Penang Education Department has taken precautionary steps to protect a 12-year-old boy while investigating a complaint that he was allegedly assaulted by a teacher at a school in the Northeast district. The department said the teacher no longer has direct contact with the pupil, who has also been referred to the school’s Guidance and Counselling teacher for appropriate support and intervention, Harian Metro reported today. He said the Northeast Penang District Education Office was conducting the investigation and would take further action based on its findings.

items.title: The man who built tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Long before Malaysia–China trade emerged as a cornerstone of regional commerce, a self-made entrepreneur from Muar was already paving the way. Tan Sri Lim Kim Hong inspired some of Malaysia's most iconic names, from Tan Sri Robert Kuok's sprawling empire to household pillars including Malayan Banking Bhd, Permodalan Nasional Bhd and Tan Chong Motors, as they expanded into the world's most dynamic market. A visionary, founder of i-City and one of Malaysia's most accomplished business leaders, Lim was building economic bridges between the two nations at a time when few Malaysian entrepreneurs dared venture into China.

items.title: MEF: Foreign worker transit centre must be one-stop facility to ease arrivals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed foreign worker transit centre must operate as a coordinated one-stop facility to prevent delays and bottlenecks in the arrival process, the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) said. Its president, Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman, said the centre could improve coordination among agencies and ensure a smoother, more orderly process for incoming workers. Syed Hussain said safeguards were needed to ensure transit, screening and documentation processes were streamlined rather than creating new bottlenecks.

items.title: Budget 2027: Social Welfare Dept requests increase in RM500 caregiver assistance for bedridden patients
items.summary: “We will bring this matter to the government and hope it will be considered,” he said after officiating the 2026 JKM Volunteer Convention here yesterday. Che Murad Sayang said JKM had also requested additional allocations to strengthen efforts to assist disadvantaged groups in society. He said information provided by volunteers on the ground helped JKM identify community needs in formulating policies and implementing welfare programmes.

items.title: [UPDATED] Zahid calls for forensic audit into alleged wrongdoing at Felda
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called for a forensic audit into alleged wrongdoings involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda). Zahid said any suspected abuse of power, breach of trust or governance failures must be thoroughly investigated, adding that the probe should go beyond a conventional management audit. Zahid said Felda had faced serious problems for a long time and backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in pursuing investigations into the agency.

items.title: Zahid: BN to study grassroots sentiment before deciding on Melaka polls cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will study grassroots sentiment before deciding on any electoral cooperation for the coming Melaka election, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Zahid, who is also Umno president, said views at the grassroots level were mixed and would be taken into consideration before any decision was made. Zahid said the issue of electoral cooperation would first be handled by Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.

items.title: Indonesia steps up Kalimantan firefighting as haze worsens in Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia is stepping up efforts to contain forest and land fires in Kalimantan, with President Prabowo Subianto overseeing firefighting operations. Smoke from the fires has reached neighbouring Sarawak, where several areas have recorded unhealthy air quality. "Joint teams comprising central government agencies, the Indonesian National Police, the Indonesian National Armed Forces, regional governments and local communities are conducting firefighting operations, including water bombing and weather modification in affected areas.

items.title: NexG to resume expansion after government rules out Datasonic takeover
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: NexG Bhd will proceed with its domestic and international expansion plans after the government decided against taking over its unit Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd (DTSB). NexG said the decision, announced by the National Security Council (NSC) on Saturday, reaffirmed the government's confidence in DTSB's ability to continue supplying Malaysia's high-security identity cards while maintaining security and reliability. NexG said DTSB would continue working with relevant government agencies to enhance the security features of Malaysia's identity cards and safeguard the identity of Malaysians.

items.title: Malaysia, Pakistan share diplomatic experiences in easing regional and global tensions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 23 — Malaysia and Pakistan’s experiences in facilitating negotiations to resolve conflicts were among the matters discussed during a meeting between Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir. The meeting with Syed Asim was held at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi during Saifuddin Nasution’s official visit to Pakistan Saifuddin Nasution said the meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to exchange views on regional and international security developments, including diplomatic approaches and peace-building efforts in addressing conflicts and geopolitical tensions. During the meeting, Syed Asim shared Pakistan’s experience in facilitating peace talks.

items.title: KL Club VIP room turns into assault scene: Businessman charged after foreign woman alleges beating and gun threat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — A 36-year-old businessman has been charged with assaulting a 28-year-old foreign woman at a Kuala Lumpur club earlier this month, after the case drew renewed calls for police to reopen the investigation. Wangsa Maju district police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said police referred the case to prosecutors on August 11, before the suspect was charged on August 13 under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt, The Star reported today. Annas said the victim lodged a police report on August 6, with the initial investigation conducted under Sections 323 and 506 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation.

items.title: UK's FTSE 100 clocks mild weekly gain as commodity-linked shares rise
items.summary: The blue-chip FTSE 100 rose 0.6 per cent to 10,816.6 points, also clocking a 0.6 per cent rise for the week. The midcap FTSE 250 climbed 0.9 per cent but marked its first weekly decline in six. Antofagasta and Endeavour Mining rose 5.4 per cent and 4.1 per cent, respectively, leading gains in the FTSE 100.

items.title: Fahmi: 2027 Budget to put greater focus on cost of living
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will place greater emphasis on addressing cost-of-living issues more comprehensively in the 2027 Budget, taking into account the unsettled global geopolitical situation. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said budget preparations would also consider external factors, including global crude oil price movements. Fahmi said the budget would also prioritise projects capable of resolving public issues quickly, while attracting more domestic and international investment to support the 13th Malaysia Plan.

items.title: Indonesia welcomes more Chinese investments, business: Prabowo
items.summary: Prabowo said China treats Indonesia as an equal with mutual respect, and provides Indonesia with valuable confidence and support. No force can stop the continuous rise of developing countries such as China and Indonesia, Wang said. Noting that China and Indonesia have obvious complementary advantages, Wang said China is a reliable, long-term and stable partner in Indonesia's national development process.

items.title: Civil Defence man dies after king cobra bite during demonstration
items.summary: TEMERLOH: A Civil Defence Force (APM) personnel died early today after being bitten by a king cobra during a demonstration yesterday. Sergeant (PA) Muhamad Muazam Shah Kamardin, 39, of the Temerloh APM office, died at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) here at 1.50am. Pahang APM director Colonel Che Adam A. Rahman said Muazam Shah died while receiving treatment.

items.title: Bigger dams, more ponds, river dredging: KL and Selangor plan five flood fixes on the table
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Kuala Lumpur and Selangor are joining forces to tackle the Klang Valley’s flood problems, with plans to review dam capacity, build new retention ponds and dredge rivers as part of a five-point action plan. The move comes as both administrations seek to better manage water flowing from Hulu Selangor through Kuala Lumpur and towards the southern parts of the Klang Valley, where heavy rain can quickly turn into flooding. “Selangor and Kuala Lumpur must join forces to manage water drainage from the Hulu Selangor area which flows through Kuala Lumpur and onward to the southern localities,” Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said in a joint statement today.

items.title: Sabah records biggest unemployment drop as MYFutureJobs efforts yield over 71,000 job placements
items.summary: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor said Sabah recorded the most significant reduction in unemployment among all states in Malaysia during the first quarter of this year. “This reflects the government’s continued commitment to helping Sabahans secure employment and improve their economic well-being,” he said in a speech read by Deputy Chief Minister II Datuk Seri Panglima Masidi Manjun during the launch of the MYFutureJobs X Oil & Gas Kota Kinabalu 2026 Career Carnival at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) here yesterday. Khairul Firdaus said Kesuma was also implementing a paradigm shift to strengthen Sabah’s labour market through the Sabah Talent Development Centre (STDC), which serves as a strategic platform integrating talent development with industry requirements and labour market information.

items.title: No Malaysians injured in Narathiwat blasts, arson attacks
items.summary: KOTA BARU: No Malaysians were injured after at least 11 locations in Thailand's southern border province of Narathiwat were hit by a series of security incidents, including explosions, arson attacks and the burning of vehicle tyres last night. Narathiwat provincial police commander Major General Prayong Kotsakha said two Thai citizens were injured in the incidents. He said the incidents, which began at 8pm, involved several areas in Narathiwat, including locations near the Malaysia-Thailand border.

items.title: Budget 2027 to focus on cost‑of‑living issues and attracting investment, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — The government will place greater emphasis on addressing the people’s cost-of-living issues more comprehensively in Budget 2027, taking into account the unsettled global geopolitical situation, said Madani Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the budget preparations would also consider various external factors, including movements in global crude oil prices. Also present was Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Information Department director Normaizatulakmal Tujad.

items.title: Before the next tree falls, DBKL places 200 sensors to keep dangerous ones in check
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Kuala Lumpur is turning to technology to keep a closer watch on its ageing trees, with City Hall set to install at least 200 sensors that can flag potential hazards in real time. Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the sensors would be placed on selected mature trees about 1.2 metres above ground and linked to DBKL’s control centre, The Star r eported. The move forms the second phase of DBKL’s urban tree management programme after the city completed the mapping of 25,000 trees earlier this year with funding from the Digital Ministry.

items.title: PN open to seat allocation with BN to ensure victories, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition was willing to give up certain seats to Umno if cooperation could help secure victories in states where both parties had support. Takiyuddin said Pas had agreed to let Umno contest 25 of the 36 state seats in Negri Sembilan, while PN would contest the remaining 11 under an electoral cooperation arrangement. Otherwise, how could PN win all 28 state seats in Terengganu?

items.title: Businessman charged with assaulting Vietnamese woman at KL club
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman has been charged with voluntarily causing hurt to a Vietnamese woman who was allegedly assaulted at a club here earlier this month. Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said police received a report on Aug 6 and investigated the case under Sections 323 and 506 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation. She lodged a police report at the Wangsa Maju police station on Aug 6, claiming only one suspect was detained before being released two days later.S © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia tech sector poised for extended AI-driven bull run into FY27
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's technology sector is poised for a sustained bull run into the second half (2H) of 2026, supported by accelerating earnings growth, robust order books and stronger factory loadings, RHB Research said. The firm's analyst Lee Meng Horng said recent ground checks across the technology supply chain reinforced the firm's high-conviction view that the sector remains firmly in an upcycle, which could extend into financial year 2027 (FY27). Lee expects the Kuala Lumpur Technology Index to continue outperforming as sector earnings growth accelerates from the second quarter of 2026.

items.title: Malaysian caught in Golok lockdown after bomb blasts stranded in Thai town
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — A Malaysian visitor to Sungai Golok in southern Thailand found himself caught in a night of chaos after a string of bomb blasts sent military and fire trucks onto the streets and triggered roadblocks across the border town. The visitor, identified only as Main, told The New Straits Times that key roads were closed by security personnel shortly after the explosions began. After hearing the first blast, Main spoke to residents who told him coordinated attacks were taking place at several locations across southern Thailand.

items.title: Man killed in car‑lorry collision along Bintulu-Samalaju Coastal Road
items.summary: BINTULU, Aug 23 — A man was killed after the car he was driving collided with a lorry along the Bintulu-Samalaju Coastal Road here yesterday. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba), in a statement, said a team from the Kidurong Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call about the accident at around 8.41am. “Upon arriving at the scene, the firefighters found that an accident involving a car and a lorry had occurred,” it said in a statement.

items.title: Penang Occupational Safety Dept probes worker's death at Juru telecom tower
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Occupational Safety and Health Department is investigating the death of a telecommunications worker following an accident at a tower in Juru. The department said it was notified of the workplace accident involving the worker, who died on Aug 16. The investigation is being conducted under Sections 15(1), 17(1) and 18B of the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, as well as relevant occupational safety and health regulations.

items.title: Fitch keeps Poland rating at 'A-', cites fiscal risks in negative outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fitch retained Poland's sovereign credit rating at "A-" on Friday, citing the country's resilient economy and strong external finances relative to similarly rated peers, while maintaining a "negative" outlook due to a lack of strong fiscal consolidation. Here are some more details: * The rating action comes as the nation's budget deficit widened to 141.1 billion zlotys (US$38.19 billion) at the end of July, compared with 123.7 billion zlotys (US$33.48 billion) at the end of June. * The agency expects the country's fiscal deficit to narrow marginally to 6.7 per cent of GDP in 2027, above its February forecast of 6.2 per cent, and flagged risks of additional spending ahead of elections.

items.title: Sarawak ties economic growth to ESG goals
items.summary: The recognition validates how the state's Legacy Impact Framework has redefined standards for responsible business events across the region, embedding sustainable development at the intersection of commerce, community welfare and environmental stewardship. The framework anchors Sarawak's business events sector to two core blueprints, its post-Covid-19 Development Strategy 2030 and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. "This recognition reflects the collective effort behind Sarawak's legacy journey," said Datuk Hii Chang Kee, Deputy State Secretary (Operation) and chairman of Business Events Sarawak (BESarawak).

items.title: Hit by Trump tariffs, Quebec loses appetite for quick separation from Canada
items.summary: MONTREAL: When US President Donald Trump levied 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian steel in June last year, a steel factory in Canada's mostly French-speaking province of Quebec lost about a third of its orders for bolts and fasteners in less than a week. The cuts were part of 140 layoffs by the company, mainly in Quebec. The factory's troubles reflect broader anxiety over the fallout from Trump's trade war in Quebec, which is due to hold a provincial election by Oct 5.

items.title: OSK Property partners RHB Bank to extend home and renovation loan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OSK Property Holdings Bhd has partnered with RHB Bank Bhd to extend the RHB Home and Renovation Loan to eligible purchasers of selected under-construction landed properties developed by OSK Property. The property arm of OSK Group said in a statement that the collaboration marked RHB's first property-developer partnership for the solution, which was previously available to eligible purchasers of completed and subsale properties. "This allows eligible purchasers to plan their overall homeownership and renovation funding needs upfront, instead of arranging separate renovation funding only after their homes are completed.

items.title: Libaran MP says new settlement site being secured for 28 Pulau Nunuyan fire‑hit families
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 23 — Efforts are underway to secure a new settlement site for 28 families left homeless by the recent fire at Kampung Pulau Nunuyan Laut, said Libaran MP Datuk Suhaimi Nasir. Suhaimi, who visited the victims on Saturday, said discussions were being held with the State Lands and Surveys Department to identify suitable government land near the area, with the land matter targeted for resolution within a month. “If approved, we will work towards ensuring that the land lots are allocated only to the 28 affected families,” said Suhaimi, who is also Risda Holdings Chairman.

items.title: Temerloh snake demo ends in tragedy as officer dies after king cobra bite
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Aug 23 — A civil defence officer who was bitten by a cobra while demonstrating how to handle the reptile at a community programme here yesterday, died early this morning. The Temerloh Civil Defence Force officer Sergeant Muhamad Muazam Shah Kamardin, 39, died at 1.50am while receiving treatment at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital here, Malay news outlet BH reported. Muhamad Muazam Shah was reportedly single and had an elder sister.

items.title: Electrical worker dies after suspected electrocution during installation work in Sandakan
items.summary: The victim, identified as Jai, 30, was pronounced dead at the scene by a Health Ministry medical officer. Sandakan Fire and Rescue Station Chief Jimmy Lagung said the department received an emergency call at 7.53pm before seven firefighters and a fire engine arrived at the scene at 8.03pm. The operation, which also involved five SE personnel, two police personnel and two Health Ministry personnel, was brought under control at 9.26pm and ended at 9.40pm.

items.title: Pas says it's not ignoring Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas has denied claims that it is prioritising foreign policy issues over the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party's questions on foreign policy, particularly on China and Taiwan, did not mean it was neglecting the Tabung Haji RCI. "The issue involving Taiwan and China concerns foreign policy.

items.title: Diesel subsidy improvements to be announced within a month, says Armizan
items.summary: PAPAR, Aug 23 — The Federal government is expected to announce improvements to the diesel subsidy mechanism in less than a month, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. He said the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) is optimistic that the announcement could be made earlier than the one to two-month timeframe estimated previously. Armizan said KPDN is optimistic about the timeframe as engagement sessions with relevant parties had been held and all feedback had been submitted to the Ministry of Finance (MOF).

items.title: ‘The walls shook’: Southern Thailand blasts send a scare across the border into Pasir Mas
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Aug 23 — The sound of explosions from a string of bomb attacks in southern Thailand last night was strong enough to rattle homes and unsettle residents as far as Pasir Mas, Kelantan, across the border. Residents in Rantau Panjang and Pengkalan Kubor said the blasts were not only heard near the border but also in parts of Pasir Mas, Harian Metro reported. Faridah Osman, 53, from Kampung Banggol Chicha, Pasir Mas, also said the blasts could be heard from her home.

items.title: Armizan says new e‑commerce Bill will tighten platform and seller accountability
items.summary: PAPAR, Aug 23 — The new law drafted to replace the existing Electronic Commerce Act 2006 is set to enhance the regulation and accountability of platforms, sellers, and e-commerce users in the country. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the proposal to replace the existing act was made because the previous legislation only confirmed transactions without outlining legal responsibilities comprehensively. “This Electronic Commerce Act is merely a legal framework to validate online and electronic commerce, but the aspect of accountability is not clearly outlined in the legislation.

items.title: Man suffers burns as fire destroys hotel restaurant in Semporna
items.summary: SEMPORNA, Aug 23 — A man suffered burns to his arm while a hotel restaurant here was completely destroyed in a fire yesterday afternoon. Semporna Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) chief Zainal Sinsian said the victim was taken to Semporna Hospital by the hotel management for treatment, while the fire also damaged about 20 per cent of a nearby hotel building due to heat from the flames. “Upon arrival at the location, the hotel restaurant was on fire and was completely destroyed, while a nearby hotel building was also 20 per cent damaged due to heat from the flames,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Breathe easy? Not today as Sarawak chokes and Selangor, Perak and Kedah cough
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysia woke up to hazy skies again this morning, with Sarawak bearing the brunt of the smog. As of 9am today, seven locations nationwide were in the unhealthy range on the Air Pollutant Index (API), according to data from the Malaysian Air Pollution Index Management System portal. Serian was the worst hit at 194, just six points away from tipping into very unhealthy.

items.title: Khaled Nordin seeks audience with Johor Regent to clarify MAF and Mindef management issues
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Aug 23 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin will have an audience with the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, to brief him on administrative issues within the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF). He said the audience aims to provide a clearer picture of matters arising, including His Highness’ remarks on the leadership of the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) and the Regimen Gerak Khas (RGK). In his decree during the parade ceremony held in conjunction with the 61st Anniversary of the RGK in Mersing, the Regent of Johor also voiced remarks regarding management issues within MINDEF and the leadership of the MAF.

items.title: Anwar vows stronger federal–Sabah–Sarawak cooperation ahead of MA63 meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has assured that the close ties between the Federal Government under his leadership and the state governments of Sarawak and Sabah will continue to be strengthened based on mutual respect and trust. He said this was among the matters discussed with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor in Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei, yesterday. Anwar said the meeting also touched on preparations for the upcoming Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting, scheduled to take place in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, in the next few weeks.

items.title: Anwar: ALC‑27 boosts Malaysia‑Brunei strategic cooperation and bilateral goodwill
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described the 27th Malaysia-Brunei Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC-27) as having achieved its main objective of strengthening the bonds of brotherhood and strategic cooperation between the two countries. The Prime Minister also expressed his appreciation to the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, for the warm and cordial hospitality extended to him, his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, and the entire Malaysian delegation. Anwar arrived in Bandar Seri Begawan yesterday to begin a two-day working visit in conjunction with ALC-27.

items.title: Penang’s Eng Seng keeps traditional charcoal-fired ‘kuih kapit’ alive year-round
items.summary: “We started selling kuih kapit in 2003,” Saik said. Today, Eng Seng Kuih Kapit has a retail shop along Aboo Sittee Lane where kuih kapit is available all year round. Saik Wai Fong and her daughter Quah Ai Yin baking ‘kuih kapit’ over charcoal.

items.title: Police: Seven men arrested after viral car park fight in front of Bintulu grocery store
items.summary: BINTULU, Aug 22 — Police have arrested seven local men following a fight at a car park in front of a grocery store here, which was captured on video that has gone viral on social media since yesterday. Bintulu police chief Supt Nixon Joshua Ali said all the suspects were arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department of the Bintulu District Police Headquarters (IPD) yesterday and have been remanded to assist in investigations. Members of the public with information on the case are urged to contact the Bintulu IPD Operations Room at 086-318804.

items.title: Elderly man, neighbour trapped on 14th‑floor ledge rescued unharmed by Penang firefighters
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 1.28 pm and a team of eight personnel from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station was deployed to the scene. He said the incident occurred when the elderly man attempted to exit his room through a rear window to open the front door of the house from outside after assuming that his room door was locked. John said firefighters entered the house through the front door and successfully rescued both men, who were unharmed.

items.title: NSC blocks Datasonic takeover, vows to shield MyKad and passport identity under strict oversight
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 22 — The Madani Government does not plan to buyout Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd (DTSB), a company that provides services related to people’s identity, according to the National Security Council (MKN). In a statement today, the MKN said that the stance was taken following media reports regarding the proposed acquisition of the company. “Regarding media reports on the proposed acquisition of Datasonic Technologies, which provides citizen identity services, the Madani Government has decided not to acquire DTSB,” according to the statement.

items.title: DOE tracks 68 stations nationwide, no areas report good air as haze worsens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — The Air Pollution Index (API) reading in Serian rose to 196 as of 4pm today, nearing the very unhealthy category. According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollution Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 10 other areas also recorded unhealthy readings — Kuching (189), Samarahan (179), Sri Aman (176), Sarikei (173), Sibu (162), Mukah (158), Bintulu (157), Samalaju (153), Bukit Rambai, Melaka (152) and Miri (143). Meanwhile, 57 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality, while no areas recorded good, very unhealthy or hazardous readings as of now.
